1: # BNJI.NET
2: 
3: A personal digital hub with two full visual identities: a near-black **space
4: theme** (living starfield, shooting stars, pink/violet nebula lighting) and a
5: glossy **Frutiger Aero light theme** (sky gradients, clouds, soap bubbles,
6: bokeh) — both wrapped in a realistic liquid-glass surface system. Built with
7: [Astro](https://astro.build), deployed to Cloudflare Workers as static assets.
8: 
9: > AI agents: read [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) first.
10: > Owners/developers: every configurable value is documented in
11: > [`docs/CONFIGURATION.md`](./docs/CONFIGURATION.md) — music sources, Discord
12: > notifications, board storage, access control, themes, secrets handling.
13: >
14: > Content note: this project intentionally carries **no personal biography**;
15: > identity copy is neutral placeholder text by design.
16: 
17: ## Stack
18: 
19: | Layer     | Choice                                                                 |
20: | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
21: | Framework | Astro 7, static output, zero client frameworks                          |
22: | Content   | Content collections (Markdown) in `src/content/blog/`                   |
23: | Styling   | Hand-written CSS: tokens, dual themes, liquid glass, aero environment   |
24: | Client JS | Small TypeScript modules (`src/scripts/`), one deferred bundle          |
25: | Server    | Two API boundaries (`/api/board`, `/api/dm`) + route-guard middleware   |
26: | Adapter   | `@astrojs/cloudflare` — public pages prerendered; APIs run in the Worker |
27: | Feeds     | `@astrojs/rss` (`/rss.xml`) and `@astrojs/sitemap`                      |
28: 
29: ## Quick start
30: 
31: Requires Node ≥ 22.
32: 
33: ```bash
34: npm install        # or: npm ci
35: npm run dev        # local dev server with HMR
36: npm run build      # static build into dist/
37: npm run preview    # build + wrangler dev (Worker-accurate preview)
38: npm run check      # build + tsc + wrangler deploy --dry-run
39: npm run deploy     # publish to Cloudflare Workers
40: ```
41: 
42: ## Features
43: 
44: - **Dual themes** — dark space (primary) and Frutiger Aero light, switched by
45:   the nav toggle, persisted, applied pre-paint (no flash), fully token-driven.
46: - **Living sky** — canvas starfield with smooth twinkle (no flicker), pointer
47:   excitation, shooting stars in dark mode; the light theme rests the starfield
48:   and shows clouds, bubbles and bokeh instead.
49: - **Liquid glass** — gradient edge rims, internal optics (specular sheet,
50:   bounce refraction, environmental bleed), pointer-tracked highlights and hover
51:   sweeps; graceful fallback without `backdrop-filter`.
52: - **Theme-aware cursor** — stellar halo in dark, water-lens caustic in light;
53:   inert on touch and under reduced motion.
54: - **Scroll intro** — the homepage opens with a scroll-scrubbed cinematic (white
55:   field, blue star zooming/rotating until its energy fills the viewport), with
56:   skip button, session memory and a reduced-motion bypass.
57: - **Background music** — one player, four swappable sources (YouTube, Spotify,
58:   direct file, or none) configured in `src/config/music.config.ts`; full
59:   play/pause/volume/mute/loading/error states; never autoplays.
60: - **Profile card** — link-in-bio card (avatar orb, badges, bio, chips, link
61:   rows, copy-handle block) modelled on ayo.so profile cards, placeholder copy.
62: - **Public message board** — floating bubbles (light) / star orbs (dark) with
63:   buoyancy, collisions and drag; composer anchored bottom-centre; visible-count
64:   slider; full-archive dialog; server-side validation, sanitization, rate
65:   limits; pluggable persistence (memory → KV → REST) via `/api/board`.
66: - **Private messages** — contact form delivered server-side through a Discord
67:   webhook or ntfy push; credentials live only in Worker secrets.
68: - **The Lab** — runnable experiments and small games: starfield tuner, glass
69:   bench, orbit field, Bubble Pop, Memory Pairs, Reaction Timer.
70: - **Access-control groundwork** — `ACCESS_RULES` + middleware + signed-session
71:   primitives for future private routes; honest about static-route limits.
72: 
73: ## Project layout
74: 
75: ```
76: docs/CONFIGURATION.md  every configurable value, public vs secret, how to swap
77: src/
78:   config/       music, dm integration, board policy, access rules, theme, intro
79:   components/   glass primitives, sections, lab experiments, board, player…
80:   data/         typed site content (site, navigation, projects, lab, blog…)
81:   layouts/      Layout (shell) and BlogPost (article chrome)
82:   middleware.ts route-guard enforcement for ACCESS_RULES
83:   pages/        routes + /api/board + /api/dm (server boundaries)
84:   scripts/      starfield, interactions, scroll, board physics, music, intro…
85:   server/       board stores, rate limiter, access primitives, env access
86:   styles/       tokens, glass, aero, animations, global, lab, board
87: public/         fonts, favicon, og-cover, manifest, post hero images
88: ```
89: 
90: ## Writing a blog post
91: 
92: Drop a `.md` file into `src/content/blog/`:
93: 
94: ```markdown
95: ---
96: title: "Post title"
97: description: "One or two sentences for listings, RSS and social cards."
98: pubDate: "Sep 16 2026"
99: heroImage: "/blog-placeholder-1.jpg"   # optional, root-relative from public/
100: tags: ["lorem"]                        # optional
101: draft: false                           # optional; true hides it everywhere
102: ---
103: ```
104: 
105: ## Secrets & safety
106: 
107: Secrets are **environment-only** (`wrangler secret put …`, `.dev.vars`
108: locally). The schema in `astro.config.mjs` declares them; `src/server/env.ts`
109: is the only reader. Nothing secret is ever inlined into client bundles, and
110: user-generated content is rendered inert (textContent / validated data URLs).
111: 
112: ## Deployment
113: 
114: Static build served by the Worker defined in `wrangler.json` (assets
115: `./dist`). API routes and middleware run in the Worker; everything else is
116: prerendered. See `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` §9 before touching infra.

1: # AGENTS.md — rules for AI coding agents in this repository
2: 
3: BNJI.NET is a personal digital hub: Astro 7, static output, Cloudflare Workers
4: static assets, hand-written CSS, and a small set of TypeScript client modules.
5: There is **no UI framework** (no React/Vue/Svelte islands). Everything a visitor
6: sees is HTML + CSS; JavaScript only enhances.
7: 
8: Read this file first. The rules below exist to keep the build fast, the bundle
9: tiny, the design coherent and the deployment boring.
10: 
11: ## 1. Hard rules (do not violate)
12: 
13: 1. **No new dependencies.** `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are frozen.
14:    Never add npm packages, never run a lockfile-writing install in CI-like
15:    environments (`npm install --no-package-lock` if resolution drifts).
16: 2. **Do not modify deployment infrastructure**: `wrangler.json`, the Worker
17:    entry, `.gitignore` exclusions (`.astro/`, `.wrangler/`, `dist/`,
18:    `node_modules/`), or `public/fonts/`.
19: 3. **Canonical origin lives in one place**: `src/data/site.ts` (`SITE.url`).
20:    `astro.config.mjs` imports it for `site:`. Components must use
21:    `absoluteUrl()`/`SITE.url` — never `Astro.url`, never `location`, never a
22:    hardcoded domain other than in `site.ts`.
23: 4. **No secrets.** No API keys, tokens or private endpoints in code, docs or
24:    commit messages. Secrets are environment-only and read exclusively through
25:    `src/server/env.ts` (`astro:env/server` getSecret + worker bindings); the
26:    schema lives in `astro.config.mjs`. See docs/CONFIGURATION.md.
27: 5. **No personal biography.** Identity copy is neutral placeholder text
28:    (lorem ipsum). Never reintroduce real names, locations, schools, hardware
29:    or life details anywhere — components, data, docs, blog or assets.
30: 6. **Configuration lives in `src/config/`** (music, dm integration, board
31:    policy, access rules, theme, intro) and is documented in
32:    docs/CONFIGURATION.md. Components read config; they never hard-code
33:    service URLs, limits or provider behaviour.
34: 7. **Keep the blog workflow dumb-simple**: a post is one Markdown file in
35:    `src/content/blog/` (MDX and its workflow were removed). Never introduce a
36:    CMS, a build step for content, or a second content directory.
37: 
38: ## 2. Architecture map
39: 
40: | Path                     | Purpose                                                                 |
41: | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
42: | `src/config/*.ts`        | All owner-facing configuration: music source, DM provider, board policy, ACCESS_RULES, theme + intro settings. Public values only. |
43: | `src/server/*.ts`        | Server-only modules: board stores (memory/kv/rest), rate limiter, access primitives, env access. Never imported by client code. |
44: | `src/middleware.ts`      | Route-guard enforcement for ACCESS_RULES (SSR routes only; honest about static limits). |
45: | `src/pages/api/*`        | API boundaries: `/api/board`, `/api/dm`. `prerender = false`; validation, sanitization, rate limits live here. |
46: | `src/data/*.ts`          | All site content as typed data (site, navigation, projects, interests, ai-stack, network, lab, blog helpers). Components and pages read from here. |
47: | `src/components/`        | Astro components. Primitives: `GlassPanel`, `GlassButton`, `SectionHeading`, `PageHeader`, `BrandMark`, `Icon`. Sections: `Hero`, `AboutPreview`, `ProjectsPreview`, … |
48: | `src/components/lab/`    | Runnable experiments for `/lab/`. Each owns its DOM subtree + rAF loop, pauses via IntersectionObserver, has a `destroy()` path. |
49: | `src/layouts/`           | `Layout.astro` (shell: head, starfield, header, footer, boot script), `BlogPost.astro` (article chrome + pager). |
50: | `src/pages/`             | Routes. `rss.xml.ts` is the typed RSS endpoint. |
51: | `src/scripts/`           | Client runtime. `starfield.ts` (canvas engine), `interactions.ts` (cursor glow, glass tracking, magnetic buttons, nav), `scroll.ts` (reveals, parallax), `boot.ts` (single entry, started by `Layout.astro`). |
52: | `src/styles/`            | `tokens.css` (every design value), `glass.css`, `animations.css`, `global.css`, `lab.css` (imported only by the lab page). |
53: | `src/content/blog/`      | Posts. Schema in `src/content.config.ts`. Read posts only via `src/data/blog.ts`. |
54: 
55: Section components are one concern each; pages compose them in order. Never
56: build a monolithic page template with inline content — put content in
57: `src/data/`, structure in components.
58: 
59: ## 3. Content rules
60: 
61: - Frontmatter fields: `title`, `description`, `pubDate`, optional `heroImage`,
62:   `tags`, `draft`. Schema in `src/content.config.ts`.
63: - Listings, RSS (`src/pages/rss.xml.ts`) and the pager all go through
64:   `src/data/blog.ts` (`getBlogPosts()`, `postUrl()`); never call
65:   `getCollection()` directly in a page.
66: - Posts must contain real writing, not lorem ipsum. Placeholders get deleted.
67: - Internal links use trailing slashes (`/projects/`, `/blog/<slug>/`).
68: 
69: ## 4. Styling rules
70: 
71: - Every colour/spacing/radius/elevation/z-index/duration/easing is a custom
72:   property in `src/styles/tokens.css`. **No new hex values outside tokens.**
73: - Surfaces use the glass system: `data-glass="…"` variants or the `GlassPanel`
74:   / `GlassButton` components. Do not hand-roll `backdrop-filter`.
75: - Chips and small elements that would stack blur layers must not use
76:   `backdrop-filter` (see `glass.css` comments).
77: - Animations: transform/opacity only (compositor-friendly). Anything that hides
78:   content before JS runs must be behind the `html.js` class guard, and must be
79:   neutralised under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Keep the `forced-colors` fallback
80:   working.
81: - Type: three voices only — display (system geometric), body (Atkinson
82:   Hyperlegible, self-hosted), mono (system mono). Sizes/steps come from tokens.
83: - TWO THEMES: `:root` = dark space, `[data-theme='light']` = Frutiger Aero.
84:   Component CSS may branch on `html[data-theme=...]` for *visual voice*
85:   (bubble vs star, halo material) but never for layout or content, and never
86:   with hard-coded colours — both voices read tokens. New effects must degrade
87:   in both themes and under reduced motion.
88: 
89: ## 5. JavaScript & performance rules
90: 
91: - Client code enters through `boot()` only. New behaviour = new function in an
92:   existing `src/scripts/` module (or a new module added to `boot.ts`), wrapped
93:   in the same try/catch style.
94: - All loops: `requestAnimationFrame`, capped, and paused when offscreen
95:   (IntersectionObserver) or hidden (`visibilitychange`). Provide `destroy()`.
96: - Pointer/cursor effects are gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` in
97:   CSS and on a pointer-type check in TS; touch devices get a static sky.
98: - Canvas starfield density scales with viewport area; never render more stars
99:   on a phone than the engine's mobile budget.
100: - Images: prefer SVG; raster images live in `public/` and are referenced
101:   root-relative. Social card is `public/og-cover.png` (source: `og-cover.svg`).
102: 
103: ## 6. Accessibility rules
104: 
105: - Landmarks on every page: `header` (nav dock), `main#main`, `footer`, labelled
106:   `nav`s. One `h1` per page. Skip link targets `#main`.
107: - Active nav item gets `aria-current="page"`; the mobile toggle manages
108:   `aria-expanded` and closes on Escape/outside click.
109: - Decorative nodes (canvas, glow, icons inside labelled links) are
110:   `aria-hidden="true"`. Interactive controls need a visible label or
111:   `aria-label`; sliders pair with `<label>` elements.
112: - Body text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 against glass surfaces; focus states visible
113:   (`:focus-visible` ring in tokens).
114: 
115: ## 7. Verification before finishing any change
116: 
117: ```bash
118: npm run build          # must pass, no new warnings
119: npx tsc --noEmit       # must be clean
120: npm run check          # build + tsc + wrangler deploy --dry-run
121: ```
122: 
123: Then sanity-grep the output:
124: 
125: ```bash
126: grep -rIl "example.com\|localhost" dist/client --include="*.html" --include="*.xml"   # must be empty
127: grep -rniI "benjamin\|emond\|cegep\|rtx 4070" src public docs README.md AGENTS.md      # must be empty (no personal info)
128: grep -o "https://bnji.net" dist/client/sitemap-0.xml | head -1                        # canonical origin
129: ```
130: 
131: New routes must appear in `dist/client/sitemap-0.xml` (unless `noindex`).
132: Headless browsers are unavailable in most sandboxes here: verify structurally
133: (built HTML, jsdom assertions) and rely on the dev server for visual checks.
134: 
135: ## 8. House style
136: 
137: - Tabs for indentation in `.astro`/`.ts`/`.css`; single quotes in TS.
138: - Component files `PascalCase.astro`; CSS classes kebab-case with a component
139:   prefix (`.lab-experiment__title`); data files kebab-case `.ts`.
140: - Comments explain *why*, including the failure a guard prevents. Keep the
141:   block comment at the top of each component accurate when you change it.
142: - Do not rewrite unrelated files; keep diffs surgical. Do not delete the
143:   starter's useful bones (content collections, RSS, sitemap) — they are product
144:   features.

I'll analyze the project systematically without making any changes.

## Project Overview

**Framework & Runtime Stack:**

The project uses **Astro 7**, a static site generator framework. It's deployed to **Cloudflare Workers** using the `@astrojs/cloudflare` adapter. The project follows a "no UI framework" philosophy - no React, Vue, or Svelte. The rendering is pure HTML + CSS with minimal TypeScript client-side enhancements.

## Major Directories & Their Purposes

Based on the repository structure and AGENTS.md documentation:

1. **`src/config/`** - All owner-facing configuration: music sources, DM integration, board policy, access rules, theme settings, and intro settings. Public values only.

2. **`src/components/`** - Astro components including primitives (GlassPanel, GlassButton, SectionHeading, etc.) and section components (Hero, AboutPreview, ProjectsPreview, etc.)

3. **`src/layouts/`** - App shells: `Layout.astro` (main shell with header, footer, starfield) and `BlogPost.astro` (article chrome)

4. **`src/pages/`** - Route definitions, API endpoints (`/api/board`, `/api/dm`), and RSS feed

5. **`src/data/`** - Typed site content as structured data (site info, navigation, projects, interests, AI stack, network, lab, blog helpers)

6. **`src/scripts/`** - Client runtime modules: starfield, interactions, scroll animations, boot script

8. **`src/styles/`** - CSS tokens, glass system, animations, global styles

10. **`public/`** - Static assets (fonts, images, favicon, manifest)

## Main Application Architecture

The application follows a component-based architecture:

- **Entry Point**: `src/layouts/Layout.astro` serves as the shell for all pages
- **Page Composition**: Pages in `src/pages/` compose section components
- **Data Flow**: Components read from typed data in `src/data/`, not directly from content collections
- **Client Enhancement**: JavaScript enters through a single `boot()` function in `src/scripts/boot.ts`
- **Dual Themes**: Dark space theme (primary) and Frutiger Aero light theme, managed via CSS custom properties
- **Server Boundaries**: API routes (`/api/board`, `/api/dm`) handle server-side operations with `prerender = false`

## Build & Deployment Process

1. **Development**: `npm run dev` starts Astro's dev server with HMR
2. **Build**: `npm run build` compiles to static output in `dist/`
3. **Preview**: `npm run preview` builds then runs `wrangler dev` for Worker-accurate preview
4. **Verification**: `npm run check` runs build + TypeScript check + Wrangler dry-run
5. **Deployment**: `npm run deploy` publishes to Cloudflare Workers using `wrangler.json` configuration

The project is deployed as static assets served by a Cloudflare Worker, with API routes running server-side in the Worker environment.
